newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard PCs led 1996 Pentium Pro sales.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard PCs led 1996 Pentium Pro sales.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co.'s Vectra line of personal computers were the best-selling PCs using Intel Corp.'s Pentium Pro chips in the United States last year, according to data from market reseacher Audits and Surveys Worldwide.

The research firm said on Monday that 1996 sales data showed HP Vectra PCs were the best-selling Pentium Pro-based brand among corporate buyers, who account for 99 percent of Pentium Pro sales in the United States.
The report said Palo Alto, California-based Hewlett-Packard held a 44 percent share of the U.S. Pentium Pro market, compared with Houston-based Compaq Computer Corp.'s 39 percent.
Dell Computer Corp.'s share amounted to seven percent and Gateway 2000 Inc.'s share was three percent, with remaining slivers divided among a variety of other computer makers.
New York-based Audits and Surveys Worldwide is a U.S. sales tracking service that measures actual sales data from more than 2,000 dealer and retail storefronts.

Pentium Pros are Intel's top-of-the-line processors aimed at high-performance corporate and professional users, but they currently represent only a fraction of overall PC chip sales, which remain dominated by older Pentium technology, used in PCs aimed at cost-conscious corporate and home computer users.

While Hewlett-Packard has become the fastest growing PC maker in recent years, most surveys show it still lags behind Compaq, International Business Machines Corp., Apple Computer Inc., Packard-Bell and others in terms of overall sales.
But the new survey highlights Hewlett-Packard's lead at the high end of the PC market, made up largely of corporate computer buyers hungry for speedy chips capable of running the fastest Intel chips.

Recent surveys have listed Hewlett-Packard as fourth or fifth in terms of overall corporate PC sales and sixth or seventh in terms of total corporate and home computer sales, a Hewlett-Packard spokesman said.
